title: Morphisms between formal spectra come from continuous ring maps
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For weakly admissible topological rings A and B over a scheme, the lemma asserts that every morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces from the formal spectrum of B to that of A is the formal spectrum of a unique continuous algebra map from A to B (statement lines 2354-2360). The proof constructs the ring map from the morphism: for each weak ideal of definition of B, the factorisation statement for morphisms from a quasi-compact object into a filtered colimit gives a weak ideal of definition of A such that the corresponding morphism of affine schemes factors through the spectrum of the quotient of A, and the universal property of the spectrum of an affine scheme turns this into an algebra map between the quotients (proof lines 2362-2369). These maps are compatible as the ideal varies, so they assemble into a map of rings, which is continuous because the preimage of each weak ideal of definition of B contains one of A, and the identity with the formal spectrum of that map holds by construction (proof lines 2369-2378). The claim is H2: the argument produces the ring map from compatible quotient maps and verifies both continuity and the identification with the given morphism, each with its own reason.
